sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.

By means of the the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No. 197 of 2024 at Police Station- Shikohabad, District- Firozabad under Sections 498A, 306 I.P.C.
The applicant is in jail since 09.08.2024.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 05.09.2024.
The following arguments made by Sri Dinesh Singh Yadav, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Sri Chandan Agrawal, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The applicant is the brother-in-law of the deceased.
2.
The husband of the applicant resided in Delhi for his livelihood.

1
3. During the long period of separation from his family the wife of the applicant started an extra marital affair.
The said illicit relationship of the deceased was exposed.
4. The deceased became depressed on account of ensuing humiliation.
5. On the fateful day she succumbed to depression and took the extreme step of ending her life.
She committed suicide by hanging.
6. The postmortem report opines the cause of death as asphyxia due to antemortem hanging.

7. Injuries depicted in the postmortem report consistent with hanging are:
(i) Nature of ligature mark.
(ii). The hyoid bone was intact.
8.
The applicant did not aid or abet the suicide.
9. Prosecution evidence do not connect the applicant with the offence.

10. The applicant claims congruency in role and seeks parity in relief granted to the co-accused person Arvind @ Bantoo who has been enlarged on bail by this Court by order dated 01.07.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 23078 of 2024.
11.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 23078 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
12. The applicant is not flight risk.
The applicant being law abiding citizen have always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of their influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Satyam be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

Satyam vs State Of U.P. on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93107457/
2

(ii) The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru.
Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. (Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
